citation: Vivekananda U, Mellor S, Tierney TM, et al. Optically pumped magnetoencephalography in epilepsy. Ann Clin Transl Neurol. 2020;7(3):397-401.
design: Single-patient case report. Two separate 30-min OP-MEG sessions, no SQUID-MEG; qualitative comparison with an earlier 5-day scalp EEG telemetry (not simultaneous).
epilepsy_and_regions: Drug-refractory focal epilepsy after Haemophilus meningitis with status epilepticus at 18 months; right posterior quadrant focus (right parieto-occipital damage on MRI); EEG interictal activity maximal at T8 and right sphenoidal.
opm_type_count_noise: Rubidium OPMs (QuSpin named as manufacturer in the conflict-of-interest statement). Session 1: 8 first-generation OPMs in a bespoke plinth (patient lying) plus 6 reference sensors. Session 2: 15 second-generation OPMs in a 3D-printed scanner-cast. Noise not measured; the Introduction cites a white-noise floor of about 10 fT/sqrt(Hz) for recent OPMs and a sensitive volume about 6 mm from the scalp, against about 3-4 cm for cryogenic MEG.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: None. No cryogenic MEG (surgical schedule and ethical constraints); comparison with prior clinical EEG only.
amplitude_result: No measured comparison. The Discussion expects a two- to fivefold smaller signal with conventional MEG, from earlier studies (an expectation, not a measurement).
localization_result: Dipole fit of averaged spikes (session 2) in the right posterior quadrant, the EEG-defined presumed focus; later resection reduced seizure frequency.
other_key_numbers: 23 spikes per 30 min (session 1) and 19 per 30 min (session 2); about 30 interictal discharges per hour on EEG telemetry; no seizure during OP-MEG; 1-70 Hz band-pass.
verification: full text (PMC7085997): Introduction, Method, Results, Discussion; all numbers checked in the text.
notes: First human OPM epilepsy recording. Sensors concentrated over the region of interest (authors' limitation); EEG and OP-MEG not simultaneous.

citation: Feys O, Corvilain P, Aeby A, et al. On-scalp optically pumped magnetometers versus cryogenic magnetoencephalography for diagnostic evaluation of epilepsy in school-aged children. Radiology. 2022;304(2):429-434.
design: Prospective single-centre case series. On-scalp OPM-MEG and cryogenic MEG in the same children, recorded sequentially (OPM first in all children, per the preprint); IED detection, amplitude, SNR and distributed source localization compared; unpaired t tests per child.
epilepsy_and_regions: Self-limited idiopathic (n = 3) or refractory (n = 2) focal epilepsy (published abstract). The preprint describes all five as extratemporal focal epilepsies with unifocal IEDs; one refractory child had a resected right temporal dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumour with a distant presumed epileptogenic zone. Per-child IED regions are in Table 1, which was not available to us.
opm_type_count_noise: 32 QuSpin Gen-2 zero-field OPMs in single-axis mode, on a flexible EEG-like cap (EasyCap; 3D-printed mounts sewn at 10-10 positions), placed around the presumed epileptogenic zone; compact OPM shielded room, background below 15 nT after degaussing, no further field compensation (preprint Methods). Sensor noise not reported.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: Cryogenic 306-channel MEGIN Triux in a light-weight shielded room (102 magnetometers, 204 planar gradiometers), restricted to its 102 magnetometers for comparability (preprint Methods; restated by the same group in Feys 2025, p. e148).
snr_definition: Peak amplitude and SNR estimated for each spike at the sensor with the maximal averaged spike amplitude (preprint Methods); the same group defines this SNR as peak amplitude over baseline SD (Feys 2025, p. e145). Baseline correction -100 to -50 ms (preprint).
amplitude_result: IED amplitude 2.3 (7.2 of 3.1) to 4.6 (3.2 of 0.7) times higher with on-scalp MEG, P < .001, in all five children (published abstract; units not printed in the abstract; the preprint gives 2.3 to 4.8 times).
snr_result: SNR 27% (16.7 of 13.2) to 60% (12.8 of 8.0) higher with on-scalp MEG (P = .001-.009) in four of five children; no difference (P = .93) in the fifth, whose head movements caused pronounced motion artefacts (published abstract).
localization_result: Sources of averaged IEDs about 5 mm apart between systems in 3 children, 8.3 mm and 15.6 mm in the other two (abstract); preprint range 4.2-15.6 mm.
other_key_numbers: Preprint only: spike-wave index 2-89%; mean distance from the reconstructed source to the closest sensor 29.4 mm (OPM) vs 57.6 mm (SQUID); OPM recordings 15-30 min.
verification: abstract only for the version of record (PubMed 35503013; publisher abstract). Methods and the preprint-only numbers from the full text of the medRxiv preprint v1 (doi 10.1101/2021.09.06.21262839): Materials and Methods, Results, Discussion. Table 1 (per child) not available.
notes: The published abstract (upper amplitude ratio 4.6) supersedes the preprint (4.8). Sequential, not simultaneous recordings. The child of Feys 2023 (Front Neurosci) is patient 5 of this series. The infant letter (Feys 2023, Clin Neurophysiol) cites mean OPM IED amplitudes of 3.2-9.9 pT for these five children (from this paper's Table 2).

citation: Feys O, Corvilain P, Van Hecke A, et al. Recording of ictal epileptic activity using on-scalp magnetoencephalography. Ann Neurol. 2023;93(2):419-421.
design: Single-patient case report (letter). 1-h resting video-OPM-MEG plus a 3-min hyperventilation; later SEEG.
epilepsy_and_regions: Drug-resistant focal epilepsy, more than 5 seizures per day. More than 600 IEDs of two types: about 70% left mesio-occipital (source in the left cuneus) and about 30% left temporo-occipital (left supramarginal gyrus). 15 spontaneous and 6 hyperventilation-induced seizures from several regions (left frontal 3, temporal 1, parietal 9, occipital 5; right parietal 2; right occipital count not legible in the text). SEEG (16 posterior electrodes) confirmed multifocal seizure-onset zones.
opm_type_count_noise: 24 triaxial QuSpin QZFM-G3 OPMs on an EEG-like cap, 1200 Hz; Compact MuRoom (Cerca Magnetics), remnant field below 1-2 nT after degaussing and active nulling. Noise not reported.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: None. Cryogenic MEG was unavailable at the time (technical issues); SNR compared only between rest and hyperventilation.
snr_definition: Seizure SNR: mean amplitude of the whole seizure divided by the mean amplitude of the preceding IED-free background, at the sensor with maximal ictal amplitude (Welch unpaired t tests).
amplitude_result: Hyperventilation raised seizure amplitude (1.92 +/- 0.04 vs 1.49 +/- 0.05 pT at rest) and background amplitude (0.69 +/- 0.02 vs 0.52 +/- 0.03 pT), p < 0.003.
snr_result: Seizure SNR similar: 2.79 +/- 0.07 (hyperventilation) vs 2.97 +/- 0.19 (rest), p = 0.43. No OPM-vs-SQUID SNR.
localization_result: Posterior seizure-onset and irritative zones from OPM-MEG co-localized with SEEG; the frontal onsets were not sampled by SEEG.
other_key_numbers: 10 of the seizures were accompanied by eye, eyelid or head movements.
verification: full text of the letter (publisher text retrieved via the DOI; pp. 419-421; the text extraction rendered plus-minus signs as 'AE'). No section or page numbers inside the letter.
notes: Cited by Shen 2026 (its ref. 12, p. 3938 and p. 3949) as evidence that OPM SNR is comparable to or better than SQUID-MEG, but the letter contains no SQUID comparison.

citation: Hillebrand A, Holmes N, Sijsma N, et al. Non-invasive measurements of ictal and interictal epileptiform activity using optically pumped magnetometers. Sci Rep. 2023;13:4623.
design: Case series. OPM (morning, seated, 15-min runs) and SQUID (same day, afternoon, supine, four 15-min runs) recorded separately; OPM positions chosen from the IED field maps of earlier clinical MEG (and SEEG in adults); sleep-deprived patients.
n_detail: 7 patients: 3 adults with deep or weak IED sources, 3 children, 1 adult with daily seizures
ages: three children aged 10-12 years; four adults (adult ages in Supplementary Table S1, not consulted)
epilepsy_and_regions: Focal drug-resistant epilepsy with previously characterised IED sources; hypothesised epileptogenic zone bilateral mesial temporal, multifocal, or near somatosensory cortex. IEDs in this study: bilateral temporal (patient 1), right superior temporal/parietal (3), right sensorimotor (4), right central/superior temporal (6); none in patients 2 and 5; patient 7 seizure with onset over both anterior temporal lobes on the OPMs.
opm_type_count_noise: Six QuSpin Gen-2 OPMs in dual-axis mode (radial plus one tangential axis) = 12 channels; sensitivity 7-13 fT/sqrt(Hz), dynamic range +/-5 nT, bandwidth 0 to about 130 Hz; individual rigid 3D-printed helmets; bi-planar coils with dynamic field compensation; homogeneous field correction.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: 306-channel MEGIN Triux Neo in the same shielded room; SNR computed on the SQUID planar gradiometers only (Table 1 caption); tSSS.
snr_definition: Z-score of each IED from a simple automatic detector at sensor level (events standing out from baseline), averaged over IEDs and reported as mean (SD), used as a proxy for SNR. Also a spike-wave index (percentage of seconds containing an IED).
amplitude_result: Not reported (no amplitudes or amplitude ratios in the paper).
snr_result: OPM vs SQUID SNR, mean (SD): patient 1, 4.47 (0.43) vs 4.57 (0.46); patient 3, 3.85 (0.32) vs 3.93 (0.35); patient 4, 4.05 (0.48) vs 4.39 (0.61); patient 6, 6.15 (0.98) with OPMs and no IEDs with SQUID. OPM/SQUID ratios 0.98, 0.98 and 0.92 [derived]. Authors: comparable SNRs overall.
localization_result: Consistent field maps and topographies between systems; beamformer virtual electrodes; no localization-distance metric.
other_key_numbers: Spike-wave index OPM vs SQUID: 6.42 vs 10.25 (patient 1; 6.11 and 6.58 for left- and right-only SQUID channels), 9.00 vs 6.76 (3), 11.03 vs 24.50 (4), 0.53 vs 0 (6). Patient 6: 3 and 5 IEDs in two OPM runs, none in four SQUID runs. Patient 7: seizure after 2.5 h of OPM recording (no SQUID that visit). Sensor balance 6 sensors/12 channels vs 102 sensors/306 channels.
verification: full text (PMC10030968): Methods (patients, OPM sensors, SQUID recordings, IED quantification), Results, Discussion; Table 1 transcribed from the Europe PMC XML.
notes: Authors list factors that cloud the comparison: dual-axis operation (a sensitivity cost) and sub-optimal placement may lower OPM SNR; time of day, posture and drowsiness differed between sessions; movement artefacts may hide IEDs in the OPM data. The medRxiv preprint (10.1101/2022.11.03.22281836) abstract adds effect sizes for the three SNR comparisons (d = -0.14, -0.14, -0.36) and its Table 1 caption states that all patients were male; neither appears in the version of record we read.

citation: Feys O, Corvilain P, Bertels J, et al. On-scalp magnetoencephalography for the diagnostic evaluation of epilepsy during infancy. Clin Neurophysiol. 2023;155:29-31.
design: Single-infant case report (letter). 30-min on-scalp video-OPM-MEG without sedation; no cryogenic MEG in this infant.
ages: 5-month-old girl born preterm (adjusted age 2 months); head circumference 33 cm (microcephaly)
epilepsy_and_regions: Focal epilepsy after a grade IV intraventricular haemorrhage (ventriculo-peritoneal shunt); EEG focus at C4. IEDs over right parietal sensors; dipoles clustered in the right centro-parietal region.
opm_type_count_noise: 26 QuSpin OPMs (17 QZFM-G3, 9 QZFM-G2), 1200 Hz, on a 34-cm EEG-like cap; shielded room with field-nulling coils (Cerca Magnetics), background below 2 nT; a 4-mm gap between OPMs and the bald scalp for heat dissipation (the Fig. 1 legend says 3 mm). Radial axes used for dipole fitting. Noise not reported.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: No same-patient SQUID data. Indirect comparison with the five school-aged children of Feys 2022 (their OPM values and their cryogenic MEG SNRs).
snr_definition: Not defined in the letter; IED amplitude, background and SNR reported separately (methods refer to Feys 2022).
amplitude_result: IED amplitude 2.5 +/- 1.1 pT and background 0.30 +/- 0.15 pT, both lower than in the school-aged children of Feys 2022 (mean IED amplitudes 3.2-9.9 pT; background 0.32-0.97 pT, cited as unpublished data).
snr_result: SNR 11.1 +/- 8.9 after cardiac-artefact removal: close to the OPM SNR of 2 of the 5 school-aged children and lower than the other 3; similar to or higher than those children's cryogenic MEG SNRs (authors' comparison).
localization_result: Equivalent current dipoles (spherical model, goodness of fit above 80%) clustered in the right centro-parietal region, congruent with C4 involvement.
other_key_numbers: 70 monomorphic IEDs, 41 with goodness of fit above 80%; cap placement under 1 min.
verification: full text of the letter (publisher HTML text, ScienceDirect; pp. 29-31; the letter has no section numbers).
notes: Lower amplitude attributed by the authors to the extra scalp gap and the large lesion. Schwartz 2025 (ref. 11) and Shen 2026 cite this letter for higher OPM SNR in infants, but it has no same-infant SQUID comparison.

citation: Badier JM, Schwartz D, Bénar CG, et al. Helium optically pumped magnetometers can detect epileptic abnormalities as well as SQUIDs as shown by intracerebral recordings. eNeuro. 2023;10(12):ENEURO.0222-23.2023.
design: Single patient, two sessions each simultaneous with SEEG: SQUID-MEG/SEEG (20 min at rest, supine) then 4He-OPM/SEEG (supine). Equivalent IEDs selected from SEEG patterns by template matching, compared singly and averaged by type.
epilepsy_and_regions: Intractable temporal lobe epilepsy with a cavernoma of the left parahippocampal gyrus; SEEG 14 electrodes (119 contacts), 12 in the left hemisphere; epileptogenic network in the left mesial temporal structures and temporal pole. The spikes seen by both MEG systems arose from the left temporal pole and the adjacent anterior third temporal gyrus (neocortical); spikes confined to the hippocampus were seen by neither system.
opm_type_count_noise: Prototype 4He-OPMs (five-sensor prototype; four 2 x 2 x 5 cm sensors on a rigid helmet over the left central and temporal regions); closed-loop triaxial operation; noise better than 50 fT/sqrt(Hz) on the radial and one tangential axis and 200 fT/sqrt(Hz) on the third (not used); range +/-250 nT; DC-2 kHz; two-layer shielded room; filtering only (2-70 Hz, 50-Hz notch).
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: 4D Neuroimaging 3600 whole-head system (248 magnetometers; reference-sensor noise compensation): the four SQUID sensors closest to the four OPMs, 2.72-3.23 cm away from them.
snr_definition: Maximum amplitude of the event divided by the SD of a baseline (2 s before the event for single spikes, 500 ms for averages).
amplitude_result: Single spike: OPM peak-to-peak 5 pT in the text (2.5 pT in the Fig. 2 legend) vs 1.1 pT SQUID. Averages: OPM -9.5 pT (spike I) and -10 pT (spike II) vs small SQUID deflections (-6 and 3.7 pT maximum); legends give peak-to-peak 15 vs 8 pT (type I, n = 10) and 9.3 vs 4 pT (type II, n = 3), OPM vs SQUID.
snr_result: Single spike: OPM 7 vs SQUID 5. Averages: OPM 6.4 (spike I) and 16.7 (spike II), printed for the radial axis; SQUID SNRs of the averages not printed.
localization_result: No source localization; signals related to simultaneous SEEG.
other_key_numbers: SEEG SNR of the two compared single spikes: 14.9 (SQUID session) vs 24.8 (OPM session).
verification: full text (PMC10748329; the averaged-spike SNR sentence and figure legends re-checked in the Europe PMC XML): Materials and Methods, Results, Figs. 2-4 legends, Discussion.
notes: The compared single spikes come from different sessions and the OPM-session spike was stronger in SEEG (24.8 vs 14.9), as the authors acknowledge. Text and legend disagree on the OPM single-spike amplitude (5 vs 2.5 pT); the Fig. 1 legend gives 265 SQUID sensors against 248 magnetometers in the Methods.

citation: Feys O, Corvilain P, Labyt E, et al. Tri-axial rubidium and helium optically pumped magnetometers for on-scalp magnetoencephalography recording of interictal epileptiform discharges: a case study. Front Neurosci. 2023;17:1284262.
design: Single-child case. 40-min simultaneous recording with tri-axial Rb-OPMs and 4He-OPM prototypes (plus 4 EEG electrodes, not analysable); statistics on 102 simultaneous artefact-free IEDs, using the one Rb and the one 4He sensor with the highest IED amplitude.
epilepsy_and_regions: Refractory focal epilepsy; right anterior temporal lobectomy for a dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumour (seizure-free, Engel 1A) with persisting frequent IEDs maximal at C4-T4; cryogenic MEG 7 months earlier showed right centrotemporal IEDs. She is patient 5 of Feys 2022.
opm_type_count_noise: 4 QuSpin Gen-3 tri-axial Rb-OPMs and 5 4He-OPM prototypes on an adaptable helmet with 89 mounts; one right-hemisphere 4He sensor failed and the other four ran at 60-65 fT/sqrt(Hz). Discussion: intrinsic noise 15 fT/sqrt(Hz) (Rb) vs 65 fT/sqrt(Hz) (4He). Rb and 4He sensors about 1 cm from C4 or T4 and about 2 cm apart; Compact MuRoom, 1-2 nT.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: 4He-OPM vs Rb-OPM (one sensor each); no SQUID.
snr_definition: Peak amplitude of each IED divided by the background amplitude 100-50 ms before the peak, on a virtual sensor (principal field orientation) of the single ICA component containing the IEDs; two-sided paired t tests.
amplitude_result: Virtual-sensor IED amplitude 7.8 +/- 0.2 pT (Rb) vs 4.7 +/- 0.1 pT (4He). Largest axis: Rb first tangential 7.7 pT (radial 3.6, second tangential 1.0 pT); 4He radial 4.6 pT (tangential 1.5 and 2.0 pT).
snr_result: 21.3 +/- 1.4 (Rb) vs 11.4 +/- 0.8 (4He), Cohen |d| = 0.8; attributed by the authors to sensor position rather than sensor performance.
other_key_numbers: IEDs counted by three readers: 1,372, 1,287 and 1,271 (Rb) vs 1,175, 1,231 and 1,221 (4He). Background in the IED component 0.5 pT for both; in the IED-free components 0.8 pT (Rb) vs 1.9 pT (4He).
verification: full text (PMC10715393; patient identity re-checked in the Europe PMC XML): Methods (case report, data acquisition, preprocessing and analyses), Results, Discussion.
notes: Sensor type and sensor position are confounded (authors' limitation). Not an OPM-vs-SQUID comparison.

citation: Feys O, Ferez M, Corvilain P, et al. On-scalp magnetoencephalography based on optically pumped magnetometers can detect mesial temporal lobe epileptiform discharges. Ann Neurol. 2024;95(3):620-622.
design: Single-patient case (letter). 10-min simultaneous video-OPM-MEG and SEEG at the end of a two-week video-SEEG; OPM IEDs marked blind to SEEG.
epilepsy_and_regions: Refractory focal epilepsy with a large right temporo-parietal cortical malformation and multiple right nodular heterotopias (preprint); most active irritative zone in the right amygdala; multiple seizure-onset zones.
opm_type_count_noise: 48 QuSpin OPMs (20 QZFM-G3, 28 QZFM-G2) = 116 channels (118 in the preprint's abstract and Methods) on an adult-sized rigid 3D-printed helmet (Cerca Magnetics), i.e. close to rather than on the scalp; 18 of 116 channels excluded as noisy. Noise not reported.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: No SQUID. SEEG as ground truth (64 of 186 contacts recorded); SNR compared only with published values.
snr_result: 2.75 +/- 2.55: lower than earlier OPM recordings of neocortical IEDs (11.1 to 16.7; Feys 2022 and the 2023 infant letter) and similar to simultaneous cryogenic MEG-SEEG recordings of neocortical IEDs (about 2 in the preprint).
localization_result: OPM source 14.1 mm from the SEEG contacts with the highest-amplitude IEDs: right amygdala (SEEG) vs right periamygdalar white matter (OPM).
other_key_numbers: 31 of 52 SEEG IEDs (60%) detected by OPM-MEG, all simultaneous; detected SEEG IEDs were larger (1918 +/- 107 vs 922 +/- 85 microV/cm, p = 8.97 x 10^-10); 60% is at the upper end of the 25-60% detection rate for mesiotemporal IEDs in cryogenic MEG-SEEG studies.
verification: full text of the letter (accepted-manuscript text retrieved via the DOI; pp. 620-622) cross-checked against the full text of the medRxiv preprint v1 (doi 10.1101/2023.10.03.23296442).
notes: Authors attribute the low SNR to depth, the close-to-scalp rigid helmet (implants precluded the cap), and nearby screws, electrodes, cables and the EEG amplifier. No OPM-vs-SQUID comparison.

citation: Feys O, Wens V, Depondt C, et al. On-scalp magnetoencephalography based on optically pumped magnetometers to investigate temporal lobe epilepsy. Epilepsia. 2025;66(7):e142-e151.
design: Prospective single-centre series. 1-h on-scalp OPM-MEG with scalp- and face-OPMs; cryogenic MEG in 9 patients (same day in most, 4 and 15 months apart in two); OPM-vs-cryogenic statistics only when both recordings had at least 10 IEDs (3 patients). TLE results also compared with 7 earlier extratemporal patients recorded with the same cap.
n_detail: 11 patients; 9 with cryogenic MEG; 3 compared statistically
ages: 8-63 years, mean 37; 4 female, 7 male; inclusion: adults and children older than 6 years
epilepsy_and_regions: Temporal lobe epilepsy. OPM IED sources in the temporal lobe: anterior 2, medial 2, basal 3, lateral 2, posterior 2. Table 2 labels include temporal pole (patients 1, 9), peri-amygdala and peri-hippocampal (8), perihippocampal (10), and T1-T4 gyri, sulci and the temporal opercula (others).
opm_type_count_noise: 43-53 QuSpin Gen-2 and Gen-3 biaxial or triaxial OPMs per patient (98-127 usable channels) in a montage that included four face-OPMs on a glasses-like structure; flexible EEG-like cap (EasyCap); Compact MuRoom (Cerca Magnetics), remnant field below 1-2 nT; 1200 Hz; PCA denoising (first 15 components removed). Noise not reported.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: Cryogenic MEG of the same centre (setup per De Tiège et al. 2008; system not named in this paper), limited to its 102 magnetometers for comparability; 102 magnetometers vs 102-116 OPM channels in the compared patients (p = .31).
snr_definition: Peak IED amplitude over baseline SD, after averaging IEDs of similar morphology and topography, at the channel with maximal IED response; Table 2 reports mean +/- SEM; unpaired t tests when both datasets had at least 10 IEDs.
amplitude_result: OPM: mean 3.3 pT (patient means 1.4-7.2 pT). Tested patients, OPM vs cryogenic: patient 3, 4.0 +/- .4 vs 2.2 +/- .3 pT (p = 6.0 x 10^-4); patient 9, 2.4 +/- .2 vs 1.0 +/- .03 pT (p = 6.7 x 10^-7); patient 10, 1.4 +/- 1.7 vs 1.2 +/- 1.7 pT (p = .31). Descriptively higher with OPMs in all 9 patients with both recordings; ratio 1.04-9.0, median 2.38 [derived from Table 2].
snr_result: OPM: mean 9.4 (patient means 3.4-21.5). Tested: patient 3, 11.5 +/- 2.0 vs 5.4 +/- .9 (p = 7.0 x 10^-3, higher); patient 9, 9.6 +/- 1.2 vs 13.5 +/- 3.6 (p = .32, 'similar'); patient 10, 3.6 +/- .6 vs 4.4 +/- .5 (p = .26, similar). Descriptively nominally higher with OPMs in 5 of 9 (patients 2, 3, 4, 7, 11) and lower in 4 (5, 8, 9, 10); OPM/cryogenic ratio 0.62-4.30, median 1.24 [derived from Table 2].
localization_result: On-scalp and cryogenic sources 6-16 mm apart; SEEG (patient 6) and the resection cavity of a seizure-free patient (11) concordant with OPM sources; face-OPMs changed localization substantially only in patient 1 (mean 3.5 mm, range 0-11 mm, in patients 2-11); face-OPMs farther from IED sources than scalp-OPMs (p = 3.26 x 10^-7).
other_key_numbers: TLE vs earlier extratemporal patients with the same setup (n = 7): amplitude 3.3 vs 6.0 pT (ETLE range 2.5-9.9, p = .05); SNR 9.4 vs 14.3 (ETLE range 11.1-21.3, p = .02); cryogenic-to-OPM source distance 6-16 vs 4-16 mm (p = .23). Mean 13 IEDs per patient.
verification: full text (local PDF of the version of record, pp. e142-e151): abstract (p. e142), sections 2.1-2.2 (p. e143), 2.3 and Table 1 (p. e145), Table 2 (p. e146), section 2.3 continued and Results (p. e148), end of Results and Discussion 4.1 (p. e149). Supplementary Table S1 not consulted.
notes: Lower TLE SNR attributed to deep location and partial coverage of the irritative zone (patients 1, 8-10). The two medial-temporal patients had nominally lower OPM than cryogenic SNR (21.5 vs 22.5; 3.6 vs 4.4). Per-patient values with fewer than 10 IEDs are descriptive only; conditions differed (sitting vs supine, delays of 4 and 15 months in two patients). The Discussion reads the tested results as non-inferiority, in some cases superiority.

citation: Ren J, Ding M, Peng Y, et al. A comparative study on the detection and localization of interictal epileptiform discharges in magnetoencephalography using optically pumped magnetometers versus superconducting quantum interference devices. NeuroImage. 2025;312:121232.
design: Comparative cohort study: SQUID-MEG and 128-channel whole-scalp OPM-MEG in the same patients (order and timing not given in the abstract).
n_detail: 46 patients; 39 with IEDs in both systems; 24 with single dipole clusters
ages: mean 23.7 +/- 8.7 (SD) years; 29 male; range not given in the abstract
age_group: young adults (mean age; range not given)
epilepsy_and_regions: Epilepsy; types and regions not stated in the abstract.
opm_type_count_noise: 128-channel whole-scalp OPM-MEG; sensor type, number and noise not stated in the abstract.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: SQUID-MEG; system and channels used for SNR not stated in the abstract.
amplitude_result: Higher IED amplitude with OPM-MEG (p < 0.001) in the 39 patients with IEDs in both systems.
localization_result: Nearly consistent source localization at the sublobar level; in 24 patients with single dipole clusters, OPM-SQUID cluster-centroid distance 12.16 +/- 5.90 mm.
other_key_numbers: No significant difference in IED detection (McNemar test); OPM detection accuracy 91.3% relative to SQUID-MEG; Gwet AC1 0.892; closer sensor-scalp distance with OPM-MEG (p < 0.001).
verification: abstract only (PubMed 40254146; publisher abstract and highlights). The article is open access (CC BY 4.0 in the publisher's Crossref record), but its full text could not be read with the tools available: the publisher's site refused automated access, and the article is not in PMC or Europe PMC (checked 2026-10-05; literature_checks.md section 1).
notes: Effect sizes, SNR definition, SQUID channel type and any regional breakdown cannot be verified from the abstract. PubMed MeSH indexing lists Adolescent, Young Adult and Adult. Indirect clues (not the article's text; literature_checks.md section 1), which point, indirectly, to a MEGIN TRIUX and the 128-channel X-Magtech system (at most probable; not used in this record): PubMed's competing-interest statement names one author (M. Ding) as a board member of Beijing X-Magtech Technology Limited, which makes the Marvel MEG OPM system (Shen 2026 used its 128-channel version), without saying which system the study used; a 2024 American Epilepsy Society meeting abstract by the same group (abstract 2.489) names a Neuromag TRIUX and a Marvel MEG, for 21 patients (median age 35 years) who cannot be assumed to be a subset of this cohort; a Beijing municipal news item (24 July 2024) on the market approval of the 128-channel Marvel MEG places its registration clinical study at Beijing Tiantan Hospital, the authors' institution, without citing the article.

citation: Schwartz D, Badier JM, Gutteling TP, et al. Potential of 4He OPM-MEG for detecting interictal epileptic activity: A comparison with SQUID-MEG. Epilepsia Open. 2025;10:1660-1672.
design: Part 1: 7 patients, sequential resting recordings, SQUID (30 min) always first, then 4He-OPM (30 min), both seated, in a standard two-layer mu-metal plus copper room without active shielding; the four 4He sensors placed where SQUID showed most IEDs. Part 2: one SEEG patient, two sessions each simultaneous with SEEG (supine).
epilepsy_and_regions: Part 1: 5 focal epilepsies, all with temporal interictal spikes on EEG (left temporal in 3, including a left medial temporal focal dysplasia; right temporal in 2), and 2 generalized (idiopathic generalized; Lennox-Gastaut). IEDs recorded in patients 1, 3, 5, 6, 7. Part 2: non-lesional TLE with bitemporal spikes and right medial temporal seizures; the averaged spike involved the amygdala, anterior hippocampus and temporo-basal region on SEEG.
opm_type_count_noise: 5 triaxial 4He-OPMs (MAG4Health), one used as a reference 10 cm above the head, four on the scalp in a semi-rigid helmet with 96 positions; 570 g; 11 kHz; noise below 45 fT/sqrt(Hz) on the radial and first tangential axes, about 200 fT/sqrt(Hz) on the second tangential axis (not analysed); 6-70 Hz, 50/60-Hz notches, reference regression, ICA.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: 275-channel CTF system (2.4 kHz; third-order gradient correction; 3-70 Hz; sensor type not named in the paper): IEDs marked on all 274 working channels, SNR and amplitude compared on the 4 channels closest to the 4 OPMs. Part 2: 4D Neuroimaging 3600 (248 magnetometers), 4 channels closest to the OPMs.
snr_definition: Maximum spike amplitude divided by the SD of a 20-s IED-free baseline, per IED (part 1); event maximum over baseline SD for the averaged spikes (part 2).
amplitude_result: Group: OPM 3.76 +/- 2.81 pT vs SQUID 1.66 +/- 0.66 pT (p < 0.01, Cohen's d = 1.28; amplitude ratio 2.3). Individually higher with OPMs in every patient with IEDs (ratio 1.4-5.3; d = 1.5-6.5). OPM radial vs tangential 2.28 +/- 1.85 vs 1.48 +/- 1.17 pT (ratio 1.5).
snr_result: Group: SQUID 8.37 +/- 6.54 vs OPM 6.72 +/- 4.86 (p < 0.01, d = 0.27; OPM/SQUID 0.80 [derived]). Individually SQUID higher in 3 patients (d = 1.21, 0.26, 0.15), OPM higher but not significant in 2 (p > 0.1). OPM radial vs tangential 4.42 +/- 2.68 vs 4.12 +/- 2.36 (d = 0.12). Part 2, averaged deep spike (23 SQUID, 20 OPM epochs): SQUID 9.0 vs OPM 6.8.
other_key_numbers: IEDs in the same 5 of 7 patients with both systems; 975 IEDs with SQUID (mean 195 +/- 137) vs 417 with OPM (mean 83 +/- 97); per patient 79/96, 276/247, 69/25, 161/24, 390/25 (SQUID/OPM).
verification: full text (local PDF of the version of record, pp. 1660-1672): sections 2.1-2.2 (pp. 1662, 1664-1665), Table 1 (p. 1663), section 2.3 and Table 2 (pp. 1665-1666), Results 3.1-3.2 (pp. 1666-1668), Discussion (pp. 1669-1670).
notes: How OPM sensors and axes were pooled for the OPM-SQUID comparison is not stated: the pooled OPM SNR (6.72) and amplitude (3.76 pT) exceed both per-axis values. The 'about 30 fT/sqrt(Hz)' floor in the Discussion refers to a newer whole-head system (Bonnet et al. 2025), not these sensors. Order effect possible (SQUID first, patients could sleep). Typos: tSSS applied in 'patient 11' (only 7 patients); Fig. 3 cited for 'Patient 1 and 20' (it shows patients 1 and 5).

citation: Shen Y, You C, Zhang Y, et al. Assessment of the utility of optically pumped magnetometer magnetoencephalography in preoperative localization of refractory epilepsy: A prospective study. Epilepsia. 2026;67:3937-3954.
design: Prospective diagnostic study (January 2024-May 2025, Tongji Hospital). 90-min interictal OPM-MEG, dipole fitting without spike averaging; concordance with the iEEG-defined epileptogenic zone (31 SEEG, 37 ECoG) at the sublobar level; diagnostic accuracy against at least 12-month outcome in 51 patients. No SQUID arm.
n_detail: 68 patients (80 screened); 51 with at least 12-month follow-up
ages: mean 28 years, range 6-60; 26 female; 15 minors (under 10 years: 3; 10-18 years: 12)
epilepsy_and_regions: Refractory epilepsy; clinical localization temporal 51, extratemporal 17; MRI single focus 58, multiple foci 2, negative 8.
opm_type_count_noise: Marvel MEG 128 (Beijing X-MAGTECH): 64 OPM sensors in dual mode = 128 channels; sensitivity better than 15 fT/sqrt(Hz); rigid spherical helmet with fixed sensor positions; multilayer permalloy cylinder plus active compensation (residual within +/-0.5 nT over a 50-cm radius); supine; 1000 Hz; synthetic-gradiometer denoising, 2-70 Hz.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: None for SNR. Reference standards: iEEG-defined epileptogenic zone (SEEG or ECoG) and surgical outcome.
snr_result: Not measured. The Discussion (p. 3949) states that OPM-MEG SNR is comparable to or better than SQUID-MEG, citing Feys 2022, the 2023 ictal letter, Schwartz 2025 and Feys 2025.
localization_result: Concordance with iEEG 90.0% (Gwet AC1 .885, 95% CI .875-.894); temporal 80.1% (AC1 .723) vs extratemporal 92.0% (AC1 .926); SEEG 89.9%, ECoG 90.0%. Centroid distance 1.98 +/- .93 cm (concordant) vs 4.12 +/- 2.66 cm (discordant), p < .05; no temporal vs extratemporal difference in centroid distance (p > .05).
other_key_numbers: Outcome (n = 51): ILAE sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 65.2%, OR 11.25 (95% CI 2.88-43.9); Engel sensitivity 73.0%, specificity 64.3%, OR 4.86 (1.31-18.00). IED counts 3-162 (median 13); 5 patients without IEDs.
verification: full text (local PDF of the version of record, pp. 3937-3954): sections 2.2-2.4 (pp. 3939-3942), 2.7-2.11 (pp. 3943-3944), 3.1-3.3 with Tables 1-3 (pp. 3944-3948), Discussion 4.1, 4.3 and 4.6 (pp. 3949-3951).
notes: Concordance counts any overlap of AAL regions, a generous criterion. The authors attribute lower temporal concordance to the larger sensor-to-source distance (mesial structures 4-6 cm deep) and to the rigid spherical helmet (p. 3950). Of the four studies cited for SNR, the ictal letter has no SQUID comparison and Schwartz 2025 found slightly higher SQUID SNR. No age-stratified results (limitation, p. 3951). Table 1 prints the female percentage as 68 (26/68 = 38%).

citation: Zahran S, Mahmoudzadeh M, Wallois F, et al. Performance analysis of optically pumped 4He magnetometers vs. conventional SQUIDs: from adult to infant head models. Sensors (Basel). 2022;22(8):3093.
design: Simulation (Brainstorm, OpenMEEG three-layer BEM) on the MRIs of 12 healthy subjects; forward metrics (topography power, total information, orientation sensitivity, volume-current ratios) and minimum-norm resolution metrics (peak localization error PLE, spatial dispersion SD).
n_detail: 12 healthy-subject head models: one adult, one 9-year-old, ten infants
ages: adult; 9 years; ten infants aged 1 month to 2 years
epilepsy_and_regions: Not epilepsy-specific; whole cortex (15,002 sources at 5 mm depth in the cortical mantle).
opm_type_count_noise: Simulated 4He OPMs: 10-mm cube with 4 integration points, noise 40 fT/sqrt(Hz), 3 mm from the scalp; 102-sensor arrays measuring the normal component (OPMn), each tangential component (OPMt1, OPMt2), or all three (OPMa, 306 channels).
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: 102 SQUID magnetometers (Brainstorm model), noise 5 fT/sqrt(Hz), 2 cm from the scalp; for children and infants an 'optimized' helmet (2 cm all around) and a 'standard' one (head placed against the helmet top).
snr_definition: Topography power: squared norm of the noise-whitened source topography, proportional to SNR for equal sensor noise; total information from per-channel SNR. Sensor noise only, no brain noise.
amplitude_result: Adult: topography power 8.9 times higher for OPMa than for the SQUID array; OPMn 3.6 and 4.1 times OPMt1 and OPMt2.
snr_result: Adult total information: OPMa 1.137 times the SQUID array, but the SQUID array 1.133 times OPMn (normal-axis OPM below SQUID). For infants OPMn exceeded the standard SQUID array in total information. OPMa advantage larger for smaller heads (age effect p < 0.001).
localization_result: Adult PLE 2.3 mm (OPMa), 2.4 mm (OPMn), 2.8 mm (SQUID); SD 3 mm, 3.5 mm, 4.2 mm. OPMa minus standard-SQUID differences in PLE and SD: 0.17 and 0.9 mm (9 years), 0.18 and 1 mm (1 month).
other_key_numbers: Adult sensitivity to the least- and most-sensitive source orientations 2.98 and 3.71 times higher for OPMa than for the SQUID array.
notes: Sensor-noise-limited comparison (no brain noise). The OPM-scalp distance is defined from the gas-cell bottom in section 2.3 but from the cell centre in the array description. The Jas preprint takes head sizes partly from this paper (docs/literature/jas2026.md, section 3.1).

citation: Westin K, Beniczky S, Pfeiffer C, Hämäläinen M, Lundqvist D. On the clinical utility of on-scalp MEG: A modeling study of epileptic activity source estimation. Clin Neurophysiol. 2023;156:143-155.
design: Simulation on one adult anatomy (MNE sample subject, three-compartment BEM): ten epileptic networks with propagating seizure activity and isolated spikes from growing cortical patches (0.77 nAm/mm^2); brain noise from a 500-s resting MEG/EEG source estimate of the same subject; visual detection by one clinician plus time-frequency analysis; ECD localization.
epilepsy_and_regions: Networks with onset in frontopolar, basal frontal, lateral frontal, central, lateral temporal, mesial temporal, insular, cingulate, parietal and occipital cortex.
opm_type_count_noise: Simulated on-scalp OPMs: 128 sensors, 10-mm cubes at 1-cm spacing, 1-mm standoff, sensing volume 5 mm from the outer wall, noise 30 fT/sqrt(Hz) (chosen conservatively).
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: 306-channel VectorView (magnetometers 5 fT/sqrt(Hz), gradiometers 5 fT/cm/sqrt(Hz)); 60-channel EEG; combined arrays.
snr_definition: Detectability in raw sensor data (visual and time-frequency): smallest active cortical area giving a visible event; no numeric SNR.
snr_result: Spikes visible on-scalp from 0.5 cm^2 patches (0.78 cm^2 for frontopolar and insula; mean 0.56 cm^2) vs mean 1.91 cm^2 (conventional MEG) and 1.87 cm^2 (EEG), p < 0.01; mesial temporal spikes from 0.5 cm^2 on-scalp vs 1.54 cm^2 (conventional MEG and EEG). Seizure onset (0.5 cm^2) visible on-scalp at every site except mesial temporal (visible from 0.79 cm^2); conventional MEG and EEG first saw propagated activity (2.01 cm^2).
localization_result: Earliest ictal activity: ECD-to-onset distance 4.7 mm (2.2-9.6) on-scalp vs 20.15 mm (14.2-29.8) conventional MEG + EEG, 20.37 mm conventional MEG, 21.55 mm EEG. Spikes: no significant difference between modalities (means 4.74, 4.75, 4.71 mm).
verification: full text (open access, CC BY; publisher text): sections 2.3-2.6, 3.1-3.3, Tables 1-2, Discussion.
notes: Single anatomy and single reader; 'detection' means visibility, not a clinical SNR. Brain noise is included, which distinguishes it from sensor-noise-only models.

citation: Matsubara T, Sohrabpour A, Ahlfors SP, et al. Quantifying cerebellar signal detectability in MEG and EEG in epilepsy using anatomically informed source modeling. NeuroImage. 2026;333:121930.
design: Retrospective modelling on clinical data: subject-specific MNE-Python BEM forward models (cerebrum; ARCUS cerebellar surfaces); vertex-wise SNR for a 10-nAm source with brain-noise variance estimated from 60 s of resting clinical MEG/EEG (0.5-100 Hz) via a uniform-source noise model; simulated OPM layouts; regional statistics.
ages: 62 processed patients: mean 26.2 +/- 14.0 years, range 4.7-61.4; 25 male
epilepsy_and_regions: Intractable epilepsy (presurgical evaluation, 2021-2022). Cerebral ROIs: frontal, lateral temporal, medial temporal (entorhinal, parahippocampal, fusiform, temporal pole), parietal, occipital, cingulate, insula; cerebellar lobules and vermis.
opm_type_count_noise: Simulated FieldLine Gen1 sensors: OPM_SQUID = 102 virtual OPMs at the SQUID magnetometer positions projected to the scalp (5-mm offset); OPM_EEG = 70 OPMs at EEG positions; OPM_cerebellum = 20 OPMs (5 x 4 grid, 10 x 8 cm) over the occipital region. Instrument noise not modelled.
comparator_and_channels_used_for_snr: Clinical 306-channel VectorView (102 magnetometers, 204 planar gradiometers) and 70-channel EEG; a matching SQUID subset for the cerebellar layout.
snr_definition: SNR (dB) = 10 log10[(a^2/N) sum_k b_k^2/s_k^2], a = 10 nAm, b_k forward field, s_k^2 brain-noise variance (Goldenholz-type).
snr_result: OPMs at SQUID-matched positions: no region (cerebral or cerebellar) with higher SNR than SQUID; deep cerebral regions (medial temporal, cingulate, insula) showed no meaningful gain. Cerebellar-optimized layout: SNR above the -23 dB superficial-cortex reference in Crus I, Crus II, VIIb, VIIIa and VIIIb, and higher than the matched SQUID subset in Crus I, Crus II, VIIb, VIIIa and vermis VII and VIII.
other_key_numbers: SQUID cerebral median SNR -32 to -23 dB (parietal -23 dB); head circumference vs sensor-distance ratio r = -0.56; distance ratio vs OPM-SQUID SNR difference r = 0.53 (both p < 0.001).
verification: full text (PMC13293240; symbols and the OPM configurations re-checked in the Europe PMC XML): sections 2.1-2.7, 3.2-3.3, 4.3, 4.6.
notes: Same group as the Jas preprint (Ahlfors and Jas are co-authors). Brain-noise-only SNR. Under this noise model, proximity alone (OPMs at SQUID-matched positions) raised SNR in no region, deep or superficial, whereas a region-targeted layout did.
